verdict.rationale: Kong's AI Gateway documents proxying of LLM and MCP traffic. It covers routing across many LLM providers through a provider-agnostic API, rate limits, guardrails and safety/DLP policies on AI traffic, and MCP traffic governance and security. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of token-based (not just request) rate limits, named prompt-guard plugin detail, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can proxy and govern LLM/MCP traffic (token limits, prompt guards, provider routing) through the platform

citations.quote: AI Gateway can proxy requests from AI command-line tools to LLM providers. This gives you centralized control over AI traffic: log all requests, track costs across teams, enforce rate limits, or apply security policies and guardrails.
The core of AI Gateway is the ability to serve AI Models from various AI Model Providers via a provider-agnostic API.
Universal LLM API to route across multiple providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, GCP Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Databricks, Mistral, Huggingface and more.
Apply safety and DLP policies to prevent toxic content and remove personally identifiable information.
MCP traffic governance, MCP security and MCP observability
